title: Self-check workbook: core/extended split, optional extended, human-readable variable dictionary
description: Split the self-check workbook 'result' sheet into the yellow-marked core keys (result) and the remaining keys (optional 'extended' sheet); make the check work in a simplified mode without that sheet; give every variable a human-readable description in Excel and in the GUI.
acceptance_criteria: result sheet contains only the yellow-marked (core) keys; the rest move to the 'extended' sheet
core value cells keep the yellow fill; extended cells stay unstyled
a workbook without an 'extended' sheet passes the self-check in the simplified mode (10 core checks, exit 0)
a workbook with an 'extended' sheet is checked in the extended mode (54 checks, exit 0)
the simplified mode reports the main fields only — the optional G-test / output-row fields are not checked
the reverse GUI defaults to the simplified mode and switches to extended automatically when an 'extended' sheet is present
every key keeps its name and gains a human description: a 'description' column in Excel and a Description column in the GUI checklist
the GUI 'Export to Excel' produces the same layout as nts.checker.write_self_check_xlsx

context.dependency_audit: Dependency graph taken from .temp/расчет.xlsx (Лист2 formulas). The core values are NOT self-contained as data: f_value needs f_avg (extended), coefficients_v.* need z_averages.*/pz.* (extended), t_tests.* additionally need S_в (N14), which is not exported at all. Making 'extended' optional is still safe because compute() rebuilds the whole model from the 'input' sheet and verify() compares field-by-field — the dependency chain lives on the computation side, not on the verification side.
context.mode_resolution: Workbook: 'extended' sheet present -> extended mode, otherwise simplified. JSON payload: the 'expected' block is a complete ComputeResult -> extended mode. The reverse GUI's Mode selector overrides the automatic choice.
context.reference_file: examples/default_result.xlsx is data-identical to the hand-made reference workbook (all 26 result keys, input, criteria, grubbs, output_rows match) — only the sheet split and the descriptions differ. The original file itself was left untouched.
context.pre_existing_defect: In the uncommitted working tree, App._export_xlsx had been dedented out of the class (an earlier session) — the 'Export XLSX' button raised AttributeError. Restored as a method of App while replacing the duplicated writer with the shared nts.checker.write_self_check_xlsx.
context.not_committed: The working tree already contained uncommitted work from earlier sessions; committing was left to the user.

verification.tests_passed: 79 passed (python -m pytest -q); new: 15 tests for the core/extended split, the optional 'extended' sheet, the simplified/full modes, the description column, the dictionary sheet and the reverse-GUI mode resolution
manual_checks: CLI: examples/default_result.xlsx -> 54 passed / exit 0; examples/default_result_core.xlsx -> 10 passed / exit 0; examples/default_with_expected.json -> 54 passed / exit 0
reverse GUI smoke: core-only workbook -> 10 rows (simplified), workbook with 'extended' -> 54 rows (auto-extended), forced simplified -> 10 rows, description column localized (RU/EN)
main GUI smoke: output panel renders the description under every value, in the current language
GUI export end-to-end: the button writes a 7-sheet workbook with the description column and the dictionary sheet; the exported file passes the self-check (54/54)
